title: throughput-cost-levers-and-price-experiment-notes
content:
Purpose: working worksheet to align hiring cadence, GPU/reserved capacity buckets, and a small matrix price experiment to probe short-term elasticity for token- and throughput-sensitive customers. Draft for finance + product ops sync.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- We model a conservative FY27 budget that ties 60% of incremental capacity spend to explicit throughput buckets (low, medium, burst) instead of ad hoc GPU adds.
- Propose a 6-week price experiment across two customer cohorts to measure net ARR lift / churn at +12% and -8% price deltas on the per-token hosted API tier.
- Headcount plan focused on 7 net hires (infra + SRE + sales engineering) phased by quarter to support Dedicated sales and reduce 3rd-party burst costs.
- Expected 12-month marginal unit economics improvement: +2.8ppt gross margin if batching and caching suggestions from Optimize are realized at projected adoption rates.

Key assumptions (read first):
- Macro: FY27 ARR baseline used = $48.0M (as of Oct 2025 close).
- Customer elasticity baseline: demand slope = -1.1 (i.e., -10% price -> +11% usage) but wide CI. Use experiment to narrow.
- GPU reserved unit economics: 1 x A100-equivalent reserved unit = $9k/mo fully burdened (power, infra, support). Burst on-demand is ~2.4x cost.
- Average tokens per request and batching uplift: batching improvements can reduce effective cost-per-token by 8–25% depending on workload. We model conservative 12% average.
- Hiring ramp: hiring lead times 8–14 weeks; productivity ramp 60% after 3 months.

Headcount plan (FY27 baseline incremental hires) — working table, hires counted as incremental additions to budget:
Role, hire_quarter, count, fully_loaded_monthly_cost_per_head ($k), notes
Finance ops analyst, Q1, 1, 12, short-term runway modeling and KPIs
Infra engineer (serving runtime), Q1, 2, 20, latency/throughput tuning and kernel optimizations
SRE, Q2, 1, 18, Dedicated autoscaling and incident ops
Solutions engineer (dedicated sales), Q2, 1, 16, onboarding enterprise customers to reduce custom engineering time
Product data scientist (Optimize), Q3, 1, 17, model suggestions for quantization/batching policies
Customer success (enterprise), Q3, 1, 14, retention playbooks for pricing experiment cohorts
Total incremental new hires = 7

Hiring cash schedule (simple view)
- Q1 hires: 3 -> ramped salaries start affecting budget in Q1 (partial month hires assumed).
- Q2 hires: 2 -> fully in run-rate by start of Q3.
- Q3 hires: 2 -> fully in run-rate by Q4.

Annualized incremental personnel cost (simplified):
- Sum fully_loaded_monthly_cost_per_head * 12 * count =
  = (12*12*1) + (20*12*2) + (18*12*1) + (16*12*1) + (17*12*1) + (14*12*1)
  = 144 + 480 + 216 + 192 + 204 + 168 = $1,404k -> $1.404M
Notes: this ignores hiring slippage and equity comp; used for run-rate delta.

Capacity buckets (operational levers) — bucket definitions and expected allocation
- Low (baseline hosted): capacity sized to cover 70% of expected steady-state requests; reserved GPUs sized for predictable cost.
- Medium (predictable growth buffer): reserved+burst policy to handle scheduled increases and canary traffic (aim for 20% of peak).
- Burst (unpredictable peaks or onboarding): allowed to use on-demand at up to 2.4x cost; target cap on spend = 8% of monthly infra budget.

Budgeted infra spend model (annualized):
Line item, annual cost ($k), rationale
Reserved GPU baseline (Low + Medium), 2,160, assumes 20 reserved A100-equivalents * $9k/mo * 12
Burst/On-demand buffer, 310, capped at 8% of infra run-rate (conservative)
Storage & network egress, 420, growth tied to embedding workloads and customer SLAs
Support & license (model weights, tooling), 180
Total infra = 3,070k -> $3.07M

Pricing sensitivity experiment — design notes (short):
- Goal: measure short-run elasticity and churn signal for hosted API (per-token pricing).
- Cohorts: randomized by customer size bucket (SMB vs Mid-Market), matched on historical token use.
- Variants: Control (current price), Up (+12% per token), Down (-8% per token).
- Duration: 6 weeks active + 6 weeks observation for churn/usage normalization.
- Metrics: delta net revenue, delta token consumption, retention at 90 days, small-sample unit economics (gross margin per cohort).
- Guardrails: revenue delta threshold = $50k incremental to roll beyond test; no model change or SLA rollback during test window; finance retains stop-loss at -$30k delta for downward experiments.

Quick sensitivity sketch (back-of-envelope):
- Baseline hosted per-token revenue (net) = $0.0009/token (after model cost).
- If elasticity = -1.1: Up +12% -> usage drop ~13.2% -> revenue change = 1.12 * (1 - 0.132) = 0.971 -> -2.9% net revenue. Not obviously positive.
- If elasticity = -0.4 (inelastic): Up +12% -> usage drop ~4.8% -> revenue change = 1.12 * 0.952 = 1.066 -> +6.6% net revenue.
- Down -8% case: with elasticity -1.1 -> usage +8.8% -> revenue change = 0.92 * 1.088 = 1.001 -> ~0% revenue lift but better adoption signals.

Why this experiment matters:
- Our current unit economics compresses on unpredictable burst; raising price could fund more reserved capacity but risks dropping high-throughput customers who are latency-sensitive.
- Lowering price may be cost-neutral in revenue but buy share; need to measure retention delta.

Risk register (short):
- Measurement noise: short windows and noisy usage can mask true elasticity. Use matched pairs and bootstrapped CIs.
- Sales/CS confusion: communicate tests clearly to avoid long sales cycles being affected.
- Ops risk: sudden demand changes require autoscale policy tweaks. Pre-run a load test by infra team.

Open questions / actions (owner, due):
- Approve experiment cohort definitions and list (Product Ops / Marta) -> due 2026-01-25
- Finalize reserve bucket sizing and commitment thresholds with infra (Lucas) -> due 2026-02-05
- Create billing sandbox and test flag for cohort toggling (Billing eng / Jonah) -> due 2026-01-28
- Run small-scale pilot on 50 matched customers to refine metrics (Finance / Aisha) -> target start 2026-02-16

Appendix: quick unit econ sensitivity table (FY27 projected run-rate)
Scenario, price_delta, assumed_elasticity, projected_12mo_delta_revenue, notes
Conservative raise, +12%, -1.1, -2.9%, likely negative unless inelastic cohort dominates
Moderate raise, +12%, -0.6, +0.6%, small upside if product-market fit on price exists
Discount play, -8%, -1.1, ~0.1%, minimal revenue lift but adoption signal

Notes to self (informal):
- keep experiment small and controlled; data will be messy. emphasis on matched cohorts + pre-post baselines.
- consider coupling price delta with committed bursts (e.g., commit to reserved capacity discount in return for price stability).
- document any edge-case billing scenarios in linked_confluence page.

Version history / quick audit trail:
- 2025-11-02: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2025-12-12: added capacity bucket numbers and rough infra costs (Lucas)
- 2026-01-18: updated experiment guardrails and owner list (Marta)

End of doc.
